name: OpenShell
description: OpenShell is the safe, private runtime for autonomous AI agents.
one_liner: A locked-down sandbox for AI agents — it lets an AI assistant use real tools, files, and passwords safely, without giving it the keys to everything.
buyer: A platform engineering or security lead at a company deploying many AI agents internally who is nervous about agents leaking secrets or touching systems they shouldn't.
business_use_cases: An enterprise IT team runs every internal AI coding agent through OpenShell so none of them can see real API keys or reach unapproved systems.
A managed-AI-agent vendor uses OpenShell as the safety layer inside its product, letting it advertise 'enterprise-grade agent sandboxing' to risk-averse buyers.
A fintech or healthcare company that must prove data-access controls adopts OpenShell so every agent action is policy-enforced and auditable for compliance.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a managed/hosted OpenShell gateway with monitoring and policy-writing support as a subscription service for companies that don't want to self-host.
Sell consulting to write and audit the access policies for a company's specific agent fleet.

steal_this: Stand up a hosted OpenShell gateway with a simple policy dashboard and sell it to small AI-agent startups as 'agent safety-as-a-service' before they build their own.
